title: Capacity runway cohort notes
body:
Purpose / context:
- Prep notes for 1:1 with Jonah and weekly cohort sync. Focus: validate Q2 reservation ask, sanity-check autoscale knobs, and agree on immediate actions to avoid pool exhaustion during the next model evaluation push.

Quick TL;DR numbers (current state):
- Global dedicated pool: 64 GPUs (mix: 40x A10, 16x A100-80GB, 8x T4-like).
- Committed reservations: 48 GPUs reserved (monthly contract). Usable burst quota: 16 GPUs.
- Avg daily utilization (last 14d): 62% overall, 78% peak business hours PST.
- Recent large eval run (2026-03-03): consumed 12 GPUs for 6 hours => saturation-moment (queueing observed).

Three forecast scenarios (simple):
1) Conservative (base): 5% weekly growth in token throughput; no additional customer onboards. Peak stays under 75%.
2) Normal (expected): 12% weekly throughput growth (internal eval cadence + 1 dev-heavy customer). Peak 85–92% sporadic.
3) Spike (stress): concurrent eval + two customer load tests => peak 110% without burst -> queuing/backpressure.

Reservation ask hypothesis:
- Ask: increase committed pool from 48 -> 64 GPUs for Q2 (12-month term preferred).
- Rationale: narrows gap to expected Normal scenario headroom, allows safer autoscale margins for 95th pct latency SLO.
- Counter: raises monthly fixed cost; need to present cost-per-token delta vs current burst billing.

Autoscale knobs to confirm (what to propose at sync):
- Target_utilization: 0.72 (sustain target across rolling window).
- Scale_step: +8 GPUs per minute (bounded by burst pool and commit).
- Cooldown: 15m after scale-up; 30m before scale-down to avoid flapping during eval bursts.
- Burst_pool_policy: keep 20% of committed pool as preemption-friendly burst (for short spikes).
- Fallback: route to cheaper quantized model variant when queue depth > 6 and predicted wait > 90s.

Operational playbook fragments (notes to iterate):
- Preflight for planned evals: devs must file "eval-run-declaration" in JIRA with expected GPUs, start/end, and contact. Auto-policy: any declared run >6 GPUs/3hrs triggers manual ops approval.
- Emergency scale: SRE oncall to trigger emergency 1-hour burst allocation from AWS marketplace region-burst if queueing > 10 and customer impact flagged.
- Canary: when adding new reservation capacity, schedule a gradual onboarding: 25% traffic -> 50% -> 100% over 48 hours with perf and cost telemetry checks.

Discussion points for 1:1 / cohort sync:
- Validation of the reservation ask: which stakeholders to loop in (finance, procurement, customer success for committed ARR?).
- Tradeoffs of 12 vs 16 month term — finance prefers longer for discount; ops prefers flexibility.
- Can we convert some A10 units to A100 in the reservation to better support our largest evals? Cost delta estimate needed.
- Are autoscale cooldowns causing observed oscillation on March 3rd? We saw two back-to-back eval waves; check autoscaler logs (DE-4823).

Open questions I want Jonah to answer in 1:1:
- Cost baseline: latest committed-monthly spend vs spot/burst per-token cost (Priya to share a one-pager).
- Procurement lead time for extra GPUs if we sign 12-month reservation (expected PO-cycle days?).
- Tolerance threshold for customer-facing latency impact (what's the product SLA we promise for dedicated customers?).

Immediate action items (owner / due):
- Priya: produce quick cost delta table (committed 48 vs 64 vs 80) with per-token cost assumptions — due 2026-03-17.
- Jonah: pull autoscaler logs for 2026-03-01..2026-03-07 and annotate suspicious scale events — due 2026-03-13 (before sync).
- Liam: draft procurement timeline options (12 vs 16 months, conversion to A100) and vendor lead times — due 2026-03-18.
- Me (Maya): assemble a short deck for cohort sync showing headroom curves + the proposed ask + fallback plan — due 2026-03-14.

Notes / rough scripts for the meeting intro (to keep it tight):
- 2 minutes: current pool state + single slide showing utilization trend last 30 days.
- 5 minutes: 3 forecast scenarios and recommended reservation (64 GPUs).
- 6 minutes: autoscale changes we want to propose and why (target_utilization, cooldowns, burst policy).
- 7 minutes: cost tradeoffs and procurement ask + decision ask (approve moving to procurement or request more analysis).

Follow-up templates (post-decision):
- If approved: create JIRA ticket 'DE-commit-64-Q2' with tagging for finance/procurement/ops and attach vendor quote.
- If deferred: schedule 2-week mitigation plan with stricter eval gating and temporary increased canary limits.

Random notes / personal reminders:
- Check with Solutions Eng about any near-term enterprise demo days that could eat pool capacity (ask Kira).
- Revisit quantization recommendation doc — there might be low-hanging wins for cost without changing reservations.
- Keep track of any cross-region fallbacks that might add latency; note in the deck.

Concluding line: gather the three artifacts before sync (Priya cost table, Jonah autoscaler annotations, Liam procurement options). If we have those, proposed ask -> procurement motion in the same week (tight timeline but makes sense given upcoming eval cadence).

-----
Edit history (short):
- 2026-02-28: initial draft with rough numbers.
- 2026-03-03: added March 3rd eval incident notes.
- 2026-03-10: refined autoscale knobs after chat with SRE.
- 2026-03-12: added action owners and deadlines.
